intent: Allow delivering to a `staging` environment as well as `local`.

edit.summary:
I changed the `deliver` action's `environment` parameter in the Authoring actions table of `SKILL.md`. It was `enum: local` and is now `enum: local, staging`.

I made no other edits. The handoff already passes `params.environment` through to Delivery's `request_delivery`, where `environment` is a plain string, so `staging` goes through unchanged. I didn't add a staging `Environment` fixture to Delivery's World section or a staging example to `EXAMPLES.md`, because the request didn't ask for them.

findings.problem: The chosen environment is never used downstream. Delivery's `preview` and `deploy` kernel calls pass only domain, commit and approver (deploy) and carry no environment. Delivery has no action that sets Environment.current_commit either. While `local` was the only value this made no difference. Now a `staging` request gets the same preview and deploy as `local`, so delivering to staging may deploy to the wrong place or have no effect on a shared environment. The request's stated purpose, a separate shared environment before real users, is not met.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Delivery Actions `preview` and `deploy` (kernel call arguments); Authoring `deliver` (environment enum) and the Handoff parameters

findings.problem: The Delivery world has only the Environment `ENV-local`, and every DeliveryRequest fixture (R1–R4) uses `local`. There is no `staging` Environment fixture and no example or scenario that delivers to staging. The new enum value is untested and has nothing in the world for a staging request to point at.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Delivery World (fixtures); EXAMPLES.md, Delivery scenarios

findings.problem: Delivery still describes a single environment. The purpose says versions reach 'the environment', and the glossary says a deploy puts a commit 'into an environment'. The `deploy floor` and the `deploy` rule apply the same fixed floor to every environment. Nothing says staging differs from local or whether staging comes before the people who use the domain. The Handoff also still passes `params.environment` unvalidated into a free-form string field, so Delivery would accept any value.
findings.where: SKILL.md, Delivery Purpose and Glossary; DeliveryRequest.environment (string); Handoff parameters
